title: Stage 9, Lesson 2: How much borrowing is safe? The DTI rule
subtitle: Debt-to-income - the ratio the bank uses, and the one you should set yourself
openingQuestion: You earn 30 million a month and already pay 3 million a month on a car loan. Under the common DTI rule (total debt ≤ 40% of income), what is the largest mortgage payment that still counts as safe?
openingOptions: There is no specific limit at all
explanation: DTI measures total monthly debt obligations against income, and the usual recommended ceiling is 40%. On 30 million of income the safe total is 12 million; with 3 million already going to the car, the mortgage should stop at 9 million a month. A bank may approve you for more than that - the limit they accept is calculated on their ability to recover the money, not on the quality of your life after three months out of work.

diagram.label: Minus existing debt = what is available for the home

realWorldExample.description: Most Vietnamese banks assess a mortgage on the ratio of total debt obligations to income (DTI), usually capped around 40-50% depending on the bank's policy - but that is the level of risk THE BANK ACCEPTS, not necessarily the level that is SAFE for the borrower.

quiz.question: Why should "the maximum the bank will lend" not be read as "the amount to borrow"?
options: Banks always want to lend less than the genuinely safe level
The maximum is set uniformly by the central bank
The bank only prices the default risk it is willing to accept
The maximum already accounts for your other financial goals
quiz.explanation: The bank only cares whether you can repay at a default risk it finds acceptable - it does not account for your need to save for retirement, build an emergency fund, or meet any other goal. Borrowing right up to the bank's maximum usually leaves very little room for those.

quiz.question: One family has a DTI of 45% (fairly high) but very stable income (civil service, long-term contract). Another has a DTI of 35% but volatile self-employed income. Which is riskier?
options: It cannot be judged without knowing the value of the property
The two families carry equivalent borrowing risk
The civil service family, because 45% DTI is too high
The self-employed family, despite the lower DTI
quiz.explanation: DTI is a static number measured at one moment - it says nothing about how stable the income is. Volatile income (self-employment) makes the real DTI swing from month to month, so the same DTI figure can hide very different levels of risk depending on the source of the income.

quiz.question: You earn 40 million a month and pay 5 million on a car and 2 million on a credit card. With a 40% DTI ceiling, what is the largest mortgage payment?
options: 9 million dong a month
16 million dong a month
14 million dong a month
23 million dong a month
quiz.explanation: The maximum total obligation is 40 × 40% = 16 million. Of that, 5 + 2 = 7 million is already used, leaving 9 million for the mortgage. Every existing debt has to come off the top first.

quiz.question: For someone whose income is a base salary plus variable commission, what is the prudent way to compute DTI?
options: On total income, including average commission earned
On the base salary only, leaving commission out
On the average of the last 12 months, commission included
On the highest level of commission ever achieved
quiz.explanation: The debt obligation is fixed every month; the commission is not. Attaching a fixed obligation to a variable income stream is the most common reason a loan turns stressful.

quiz.question: Why should the DTI ceiling be computed on income net of tax and insurance rather than gross?
options: Because gross income changes month to month, so it cannot serve as a basis for any calculation
Because banks always require proof of net income when assessing a loan application
Because only the money actually received can be used to make the repayments
Because personal income tax will be refunded at the end of the year anyway
quiz.explanation: The payment leaves your account, not the figure on your employment contract. Computing DTI on gross income turns a 40% ceiling into 45-50% of what you actually receive - and that gap is exactly the buffer being eaten.

keyTakeaways: DTI (debt-to-income) = total monthly debt payments / monthly income
The bank's maximum (usually 40-50% DTI) is the RISK the bank accepts, not the level that is SAFE for you
Volatile income needs a lower DTI margin than stable income, even at the same number

practicePrompt.question: A bank approves a loan where the payment takes 48% of monthly income - the maximum DTI the bank permits. Should you borrow right up to that maximum?
options: Borrow the full 48%, because the bank has carefully calculated that this is a safe level for the borrower's finances
Borrow less: the maximum DTI is the risk the bank accepts, not the level that is safe for the borrower
DTI has nothing to do with real affordability; it is just an administrative formality at the bank
Borrow beyond 48% if you are confident your income will rise quickly in the near future
practicePrompt.explanation: DTI (debt-to-income) = total monthly debt payments / monthly income. The bank's maximum (usually 40-50% DTI) is the RISK the bank accepts, not the level that is SAFE for the borrower - so leave a margin, particularly where income is not entirely stable.

application.title: Set your own ceiling before you talk to a bank
application.message: Before walking into any branch, write down the largest monthly payment you could still live with if your income fell 30% for six months. Take that number with you and do not revise it to match whatever the loan officer produces.
application.secondary: Commission, freelance income or quarterly bonuses should be counted at the lowest of the last 12 months, not the average.

sections.text: How much the bank will lend is not the same question as how much you SHOULD borrow.
DTI - the bank's acceptable limit, not your safe limit

DTI (debt-to-income) = total monthly debt payments / monthly income. The bank assesses against the default risk it finds acceptable (usually 40-50% DTI), without regard to your other financial goals such as an emergency fund or retirement saving. Unstable income (self-employment) needs a far wider DTI margin than stable income (civil service, a long-term contract), even at the same DTI figure.

items: DTI = total monthly debt payments / monthly income

sections.title: The DTI formula
sections.equation: DTI = Total monthly debt obligations ÷ Monthly income

variables.name: Total debt payments
variables.description: Everything: the mortgage, the car loan, the credit card amount due, consumer loans, and family loans with a fixed repayment schedule.

variables.name: Income
variables.description: Income after tax and compulsory deductions, counted at its stable level rather than including irregular bonuses.

example.title: A worked example
example.calculation: 30 million of income, 3 million a month already on a car loan, 40% DTI ceiling
example.result: Maximum mortgage payment = 30 × 40% − 3 = 9 million a month
example.explanation: People often forget the existing debt and compute 30 × 40% = 12 million straight for the mortgage. Three million a month out, sustained for 20 years, is the distance between a loan you can carry and a loan that is always tight.

sections.text: Why the bank's ceiling is not your ceiling

A bank sets its DTI ceiling from the default rate it can absorb across its whole lending book - it is calculating over tens of thousands of customers, not for your circumstances. You have no portfolio to offset against: you have one loan and one life. Beyond that, the ceiling takes no account of everything you still have to do alongside it - keeping an emergency fund, saving for retirement, raising children, and surviving a few months of interrupted income.

sections.title: The safety margin should differ with the nature of the income
sections.subtitle: The same DTI figure does not carry the same risk

concepts.en: Very stable income - long contract, public sector
concepts.def: Low risk of interruption, so a higher DTI within the range is tolerable - but still leave room for long-term saving.

concepts.vi: Thu nhập có phần thưởng lớn
concepts.def: Compute DTI on the base salary alone. Use the commission to repay early or rebuild the emergency fund, not to justify borrowing more.
Cash flow swings by month and by season, so the margin needs to be considerably wider and the emergency fund deeper before taking on long-term debt.

sections.label: Three tests before fixing the loan amount
sections.text: One: if the floating rate rises 4 percentage points, what does DTI become? Two: if income falls 20%, can you still pay? Three: after the payment and essential spending, is there enough left each month to save - because if that number is zero, the loan is consuming your entire financial future.

lines: Setting your own DTI limit below what the bank permits is how you protect yourself.
Do not let "the bank would lend it" turn into "that is how much to borrow".

summary.keyIdea: DTI (debt-to-income) = total monthly debt payments / monthly income
summary.commonMistake: Easy to skip: the bank's maximum (usually 40-50% DTI) is the RISK the bank accepts, not the level that is SAFE for you
summary.action: Volatile income needs a lower DTI margin than stable income, even at the same number
